questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the next car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the shoulder of an interstate, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if possible. Interstate traffic moves very fast, so standing or walking on the shoulder is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle breaks down?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road and away from traffic as much as possible. Turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers can see you are in trouble.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Do not wait until your vehicle is moving. Before driving, also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure items in your vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can harm children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibration and noise to warn drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and noise to warn drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to wake up drowsy or distracted drivers and alert them that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles beside and behind you. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear before you move.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's signals, even if they go against traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Two outside mirrors prevent blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure the next lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming toward you from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive if medication makes you unable to drive safely?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of anything that affects your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children riding bicycles?

options.text: Children do not have the same reflexes as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and difficult to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Watch for children on bikes on sidewalks—they may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Drive very close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan your travel time realistically, drive at the speed limit, and be understanding of other drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to cross the center line to pass on hills, curves, or anywhere you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, no passing zones, or where a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass if the car ahead stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as normal.
Greater than normal.
Less than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greater than normal.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Increase your following distance when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance, increases crash risk, and slows your decision-making. When tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Keep right if you are slower than traffic around you. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on interstates, so go to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic signal is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop unless a police officer directs you otherwise. Look and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous while driving because they take your eyes, hands, and mind off the road. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk by using a phone.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, you should still wear a seat belt.
No, you do not need to wear a seat belt.
You should wear the seat belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should still wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. Use seat belts with airbags together for the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Wait and let your body process it.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait and let your body process it.
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol. The only way to reduce alcohol in your system is to wait.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and be careful.
Quickly move to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. There may be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What happens if you drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
You will improve traffic flow.
You will use good defensive driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can block traffic flow and result in a ticket. Drive at the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, who should you yield to?

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You can complete your turn once it is safe.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, where should you look?

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left will reach you first. Check the whole intersection to make sure it is clear before moving.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fight the tiredness.
Stop and take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area to take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not a safe replacement for sleep and may make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Use both parts of a two-part seat belt system. Using only one part greatly reduces protection. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, always buckle your lap belt.
